themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Surge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints spiked to 7 this week versus 1.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 367% increase (z-score: 7.78)—suggesting a new or worsening pattern of open-air consumption in Flatbush/PLG this week.
evidence: 7 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.78, 367% spike)
Spike is statistically significant and emerged in the most recent reporting period
No historical precedent in 8-week baseline suggests sudden behavioral or environmental change
reporting_angles: Locate complaint clusters geographically—are they concentrated at specific parks, transit nodes, or commercial corridors?
Interview NYPD precinct and local business owners about visibility, enforcement response, and underlying causes

themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations & Illegal Fireworks
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints jumped to 4 this week (967% above 0.4 weekly average) and illegal fireworks complaints reached 3 this week (1100% above 0.2 baseline), both z-scores above 6.3, indicating either enforcement action or new park safety concerns in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49, 967% spike)
3 illegal fireworks complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
Two distinct infractions spiking simultaneously suggest possible event, enforcement blitz, or seasonal pattern onset
reporting_angles: Cross-reference dates and park locations—was there a specific event, gathering, or enforcement campaign this week?
Interview Parks Department and precinct about whether these are new enforcement actions or genuine upticks in violations
Community safety angle: Are residents concerned about rowdy park behavior or fireworks safety heading into summer?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 51 two weeks ago—a 1066% spike above 4.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.91)—representing the most severe spike by volume in the past 3 weeks, though timing is slightly older than this-week signals.
evidence: 51 graffiti complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.91, 1066% spike)
Largest raw complaint volume spike in the dataset, indicating either concentrated vandalism event or reporting surge
No follow-up data provided for past week suggests possible cleanup or decreased enforcement
reporting_angles: Did a specific vandalism event or crew hit multiple locations? Map the 51 complaints geographically.
Was there a coordinated cleanup response? Check with Parks, Sanitation, or BID activity logs.
Is graffiti back to baseline this week or ongoing? Current status check needed to assess if problem is persistent.

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Sewer Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints reached 5 this week versus 0.5 weekly average—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—indicating potential accelerating street and underground utility failures in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 5 root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.36, 900% spike)
Spike timing coincides with early-summer season when tree roots and water infiltration problems typically worsen
Related 311 trends: water leak complaints (424 total, 90-day period) and plumbing complaints (615) remain elevated, suggesting district-wide subsurface stress
reporting_angles: Are these complaints clustered in specific blocks or transit corridors? Visual inspection may reveal hazards (buckled sidewalks, open grates).
Interview DEP about aging water/sewer main breaks in the district and repair timelines.
Resident safety angle: Are tree roots damaging sidewalks or structures? Are there trip hazards or accessibility issues?

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints spiked to 15 three weeks ago versus 4.1 weekly average—a 264% increase (z-score: 7.98)—though timing is the oldest in this cohort, the high z-score warrants monitoring for persistence.
evidence: 15 non-emergency police matter complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.1 weekly average (z-score: 7.98, 264% spike)
Timing is oldest signal in dataset; current status unknown—spike may have subsided or persisted
Complements this-week drinking spike, suggesting potential broader pattern of public disorder or police-reportable conduct
reporting_angles: Has this spike sustained into the past week or last 2 weeks? Request updated 311 data to confirm persistence vs. isolated incident.
What types of non-emergency calls compose the spike? (disorderly conduct, trespassing, loitering, etc.)
Convergence opportunity: If drinking, park violations, and police calls are all related to same locations or cohort, that strengthens story.
